description.narrative: - Addressing root causes: Through the Urban Food Crew Concept piloted by Oxfam and its partner- CCDP in Jos City root causes of poor access to nutritious foods for women and youths and inequality in Jos food system are being addressed as the food production and entrepreneural capacities of women, youths and elderly in Jos are being strengthened. Women, youths and elderly people targeted in the pilot phase have been supported to access relevant climate resilient agricultural technologies and institutionalsupport. Additionally, to ensure increased income and institutional support for vulnerable urban farmers, market access has been facilitated through private sector linkages with Fruits<(>&<)>Veggies Nigeria Limited. People (women and elderly) who hitherto areunemployed and searching for “white-collar” jobs are now beginning to embrace urban agriculture as a means of livelihoods and business opportunity. Civil servants and retirees are also engaging in urban farming as a means of getting extra income. - Changing power dynamics: As result of increased capacity and strong social network among urban farmers the Urban food crew initiative there is paradigm shift in power dynamics among food systems actors within Jos food system with smallholder farmers now able tonegotiate favorable conditions for themselves using collective bargaining power when engaging with diverse stakeholders (public and private sector). This has resulted in increased income for urban farmers and weakening the influence of middle-men within the food value chain. Urban farmers are now able toenjoy more benefits from their labor. - Changing social norms: Major food producing local governments around Jos city in Plateau State were recently attacked by criminal elements on the eve Christmas in2023. This attacks on food producing communities has resultedin a increased rural-urban migration leading to a rapid population growth in Jos city and its environs. A major impact of this increase in population is increased urban food insecurity whichisexacerbated by a social believe that food production is a rural phenomenon. The Urban Food Crew concept pilot implementation in Jos city is a proof that food production is not a rural phenomenon but rather a phenomenon which can be done in urban and peri-urban areas to improve food security and address the problem of hunger in urban areas particularly at a time when urban and peri-urban areas are experiencing rapid population growth. The outcome of the pilot implementation of the Urban Food Crew conceptin Jos city already stimulate the interest of the Plateau State government in urban agricultural development with the state expressing willingness to work with the team to develop a strategic Urban Food Systems Development Policy for Plateau State andestablish a Urban Agriculture technical working group. The is an indication that effective implementation of the concept could improve food availability in urban and peri-urban areas. Ensuring gender equity: By increasing opportunity for women, youthsand elderly people to profitably produce, process and distribute locally nutritious foods in Jos city and its environ using climate smart agricultural practices irrespective gender orientation as well as religious, ethnic, and racial background, the Urban Food Crew Concept is promoting gender equity within the food system in Jos city.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
